column3: roast S32-list/sort.t · S32-list/reduce.t (a block called with TWO arguments -- a comparator and an accumulator)
column8: hq_T 2026-09-13 (MODE NONET, the Raku ladder seat). THE GAP RUNG 15 LEFT HONESTLY OPEN and rung 17 unblocked: rung 15 witnessed .map/.grep/.first, which call their block with ONE element at a time, and named .sort/.reduce as a DIFFERENT shape it was not covering -- a block called with TWO arguments. Rung 17 (<=>, cmp, leg) was the prerequisite, since a comparator has nothing to return without an Order. All 5 forms witnessed, refs oracle-cut by rakudo-local 2026.05 through util_add_ladder_witness.py. GREEN BOTH MODES 10/10; full ladder 0..18 reads 184/184 over 92 witnesses. PROVEN TO FAIL ONCE: with only two_arg_block_reduce_mul's ref corrupted the rung reads 8/10 and BOTH reds name that witness. ALL FIVE FORMS WERE MEASURED RED BEFORE THE CURE. THE TWO DEFECTS, which are one shape: .sort(BLOCK) IGNORED ITS COMPARATOR ENTIRELY -- it parsed, the block arrived in the runtime as args[1] DT_BLK, and __rk_arr_sort simply never looked at it, so @n.sort({ $^b <=> $^a }) returned ASCENDING. A SILENT WRONG ANSWER, not an error, which is why no board caught it. .reduce(BLOCK) was not in the methcall array-method set at all and returned EMPTY with rc=0. Cured with a block-taking __rk_arr_sort arm placed BEFORE the blockless one (which matches nargs>=1 and would have swallowed it) and a new Raku-own __rk_arr_reduce, both calling the block through the g_call_args/rt_call_proc_descr path that __rk_arr_first already used -- the rung-15 precedent, so no new mechanism. The comparator's return is read with to_real, which is why an Order works (it numifies to -1/0/1) AND so does a plain Int comparator like { $^b - $^a }. CONTROL ARMS: blockless .sort and .sort with an ASCENDING comparator both still correct, all seven per-language smoke gates green. NOT IN THIS RUNG, named honestly: $^a.chars is a PARSE ERROR (a method call on a placeholder variable), so no sort-by-computed-key form could be witnessed here -- that is a rung of its own.

ALL SIX FORMS MEASURED RED BEFORE THE CURE (a parse error each, both modes, parse-level). ⛔ THE CONSTRUCT IS NOT WHAT RUNG 18 GUESSED, AND THE RUNG IS NAMED FOR WHAT IT MEASURED, NOT FOR THE GUESS: it is nothing to do with placeholders. $_ breaks identically ($_.uc), an ordinary lexical breaks identically ($s.uc), and $^a.uc() WITH PARENS WORKED THE WHOLE TIME. The real class is A PARENLESS METHOD CALL AS A BLOCK'S FINAL SEMICOLON-LESS EXPRESSION -- `{ $^a.chars; }` with a semicolon always parsed, `{ $^a.chars }` never did. THE CAUSE: a shift/reduce conflict on '.' after VAR_SCALAR. The grammar carried a statement-level `scalar_methcall` nonterminal whose three arms all began VAR_SCALAR '.' IDENT, so on seeing a scalar followed by '.' bison preferred SHIFT into that path over reducing VAR_SCALAR to atom -- committing to a statement shape that can never continue as an expression, and dying at the '}' or at the '<=>'. LALR state merging is why a `sub` body broke too, though sub_body never carried those arms. THE CURE DELETED CODE RATHER THAN ADDING AN ARM: scalar_methcall was a byte-for-byte duplicate of `call_expr : atom '.' meth_name` that existed only to serve ten stmt arms, every one of them redundant with its `expr` twin (`expr ';'`, `expr KW_IF expr ';'`, ...). Deleting the nonterminal, those ten arms and two redundant block arms, and repointing the two genuine FIELD-ASSIGN rules ($p.x = 5) off VAR_SCALAR onto `atom '.' meth_name '=' expr` and `call_expr '.' meth_name '=' expr`, removes the conflict at its source. GRAMMAR COST: shift/reduce 123 -> 123, reduce/reduce 13 -> 13, and ZERO useless rules -- an intermediate draft using a bare `call_expr '=' expr` DID shadow `%h<key> = v` into a useless rule, which bison reported and which is why the lvalue rule is spelled precisely instead of generally. CONTROL ARMS: a PARSE CENSUS OF ALL 912 RUNGS ENTRIES, run on the HEAD binary and on the cured binary and diffed -- 882 PARSED / 30 PARSEFAIL on BOTH, ZERO entries changed status in either direction. The 30 are pre-existing (BEGIN/END/ENTER/LEAVE and the other statement prefixes, :colon-calls, `our`, the sequence operator). Note what that zero also says: the rungs contains NO witness of this construct at all, so it could never have caught it -- the same thing rung 17 found for <=>. Full ladder 0..19 and make preflight are recorded in the ledger.

column8: hq_T 2026-09-13 (MODE NONET, the Raku ladder seat). THE ONE FORM RUNG 19'S ABLATION LEFT RED. ⛔ AND THE RUNG IS NAMED FOR WHAT IT MEASURED, NOT FOR WHAT THE BATON PREDICTED -- the baton called it 'a parenthesised VARIABLE before a dot'; `($s).uc` at top level WORKED THE WHOLE TIME, and so did `(($a)).Str`, `($x + 1)` and `(1,2)`. THE REAL CLASS IS A PARENTHESISED GROUP WHOSE FIRST ELEMENT IS A SCALAR VARIABLE, IN EXPRESSION POSITION: `($x);` and `($x, $y);` are parse errors while `($x) = 7;` parses, which is the tell. THE CAUSE, read off bison's own report rather than guessed: a REDUCE/REDUCE conflict in state 235 (reached from state 70 on VAR_SCALAR, i.e. `( $x`), between `scalar_list: VAR_SCALAR` and `atom: VAR_SCALAR` with lookahead `)`. yacc resolves reduce/reduce by grammar ORDER, scalar_list is declared first, so the LIST-ASSIGNMENT STATEMENT RULE `'(' scalar_list ')' '=' expr ';'` STOLE EVERY parenthesised group starting with a scalar and then demanded an `=` that a mere expression does not have. That is why it is nothing to do with dots, blocks or placeholders: after `say` or `my` the conflict state is never entered, which is exactly why `say ($x, $y).join` was already green and the same text at statement start was not. THE CURE ADDS ONE NONTERMINAL AND NO ARM: `paren_group` carries the four parenthesis shapes ONCE, `atom` reduces it, and the statement rule now reads `paren_group '=' expr ';'` -- so the group is built BEFORE the parser chooses statement-vs-expression, and the choice becomes an ordinary shift/reduce on `=` that shift resolves correctly. GRAMMAR COST: shift/reduce 123 -> 123, reduce/reduce 13 -> 11 (exactly state 235's two, nothing else moved), ZERO useless rules. ⛔ A SECOND CURE WAS REQUIRED TO WITNESS THIS AT STATEMENT TOP LEVEL AND IT IS NAMED HERE RATHER THAN FOLDED IN: `.say` and `.print` AS METHODS parsed and then SILENTLY PRINTED NOTHING at rc=0 -- `$x.say`, `"ab".say`, `@a.say` all empty, a silent wrong answer no board could see. lower_raku.c now lowers a no-arg `.say`/`.print` methcall through the SAME rk_write/rk_writes/rk_write_arr/rk_write_list choice the `say` STATEMENT already makes. ⛔⭐ THAT CURE REGRESSED A RUNGS ENTRY AND THE AFFECTED-POPULATION ARM IS WHAT CAUGHT IT: `class_method_say_6` declares `method say() { return 7 }`, and the rewrite hijacked the user's own method -- measured RED, then cured by having the rewrite YIELD when the program declares a say/print method of its own (a flag set in the class pre-pass rk_register_classes, read at the methcall site). A cure that trades one program for another never lands (CEO-589), and I only knew because I grepped the rungs for the four lines that could reach the change instead of trusting a green board. CONTROL ARMS: (1) A PARSE + AST-FINGERPRINT CENSUS OF ALL 918 PRE-EXISTING RUNGS ENTRIES on the HEAD binary and the cured binary, diffed -- 888 PARSED / 30 PARSEFAIL on both, status_changed=0, AND ast_moved=0 by md5. ⭐ THE SECOND COLUMN IS hq_I'S CORRECTION APPLIED TO MYSELF: a status-only census cannot tell 'nothing disturbed' from 'nothing reached', so the md5 is what proves the rungs contains NO witness of this construct at all and could never have caught it -- the same thing rung 17 found for `<=>` and rung 19 for the parenless methcall. The evidence that the change is LIVE is not the census, it is the seven forms flipping red->green. (2) all seven per-language smoke gates green; (3) make preflight 44 arms 0 red; (4) parser-generated-files-in-sync GREEN, the grammar and its committed bison output landing together; (5) `($x) = 7;` and `my ($a,$b) = 1,2;` both still correct, the lvalue the conflict was protecting. ALL SEVEN FORMS MEASURED RED ON THE HEAD BINARY BEFORE THE CURE (the HEAD binary had to be rebuilt to measure that: the raku parser lives in libscrip_rt.so, so md5 of `scrip` is unchanged by a grammar edit and comparing it answered a narrower question than I asked). GREEN BOTH MODES 14/14; full ladder 0..20 reads 210/210 over 105 witnesses. PROVEN TO FAIL ONCE: with only paren_group_chained's ref corrupted the rung reads 12/14 and BOTH reds name that witness. NOT IN THIS RUNG, named honestly: `benchmark_rc-self-describing-numbers` uses a bare `.say` statement modifier and is STILL RED -- measured identically red on the HEAD binary, so pre-existing, not mine; and a block that reads an OUTER LEXICAL (`{ ($x).Str }` for a `my $x` outside it) now parses and hits the escaping-closure limitation instead of a parse error, which is the known ask, not this rung.
